text.p: Tropical cyclone 05a is causing some heavy rain in south Gujarat India with potential flooding. The main impact is shipping off the coast and in the north Arabian sea during today and Saturday. The system will be weakening.

Tropical cyclone 06B in the Bay of Bengal will be an increasing risk to shipping today and Saturday as winds increase to about 65 mph. It is expected to move into north Andhra Pradesh in less than 48 hours. Coastal areas can expect a storm surge and strong winds. Inland areas can expect heavy rain and flooding with possible mudslides. The risk would be to property and also the rice crop.

Typhoon Carlo, with 85 mph winds, is mainly a risk to shipping as it moves out to sea and becomes extratropical during today and Saturday. It is currently about 530 miles southeast of Tokyo Japan and moving rapidly towards the north-northeast.

Hurricane Lili is mainly a threat to shipping during today and Saturday. It is located about 850 miles west-southwest of the Azores and moving towards the northeast. It may however become somewhat of a risk to the British Isles late in this weekend or Monday. At that time it would be an extratropical low but it could still cause heavy rain and wind.
